subject.title: feat(agents): agent-controlled session status, attention, and TTL in the sessions tool

question: Should agents receive a stable model-facing `sessions.patch` contract for transient sidebar status notes and attention, beyond the existing automatic attention states?
rationale: This is a new agent capability with persisted session-state semantics and user-visible precedence, so implementation quality alone cannot determine the intended long-term product contract.

options.title: Sponsor the agent-declared contract
options.body: Keep the three additive fields and require real-gateway lifecycle proof before merge so the behavior becomes an intentional supported capability.

options.title: Keep attention automatic only
options.body: Do not add agent-declared status and attention controls; retain the existing question, approval, and failure-derived sidebar states.

options.title: Narrow the scope first
options.body: Retain only a transient status note or another smaller explicitly approved subset, with its clearing rules documented and proven.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the agent-declared contract
recommendation.body: Keep the three additive fields and require real-gateway lifecycle proof before merge so the behavior becomes an intentional supported capability.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged adjacent sidebar-attention and narration work, plus this proposed extension, make `steipete` the strongest available history-based routing candidate.
